html:
The capital of Rajasthan in India, founded in 1727 by Sawai Jai Singh II, ruler of the Rajput kingdom of Amber.

Jai Singh moved his court down from the hill fort of Amber to the plain. With the architect Vidyadhar Bhattacharya he laid out a new city on a grid of wide straight streets and rectangular blocks, following old Indian rules of planning, with walls, gates and markets placed by design. It was one of the first planned cities of early modern India, built as the Mughal Empire weakened and regional rulers grew bolder.

Jai Singh was also a keen astronomer and built the Jantar Mantar observatory beside his palace. The pink colour that gives the city its nickname came later, in 1876, when buildings were painted to welcome the Prince of Wales. The Hawa Mahal, the "palace of winds", was added in 1799. The walled city became a World Heritage Site in 2019.
sum: The capital of Rajasthan in India, founded in 1727 by Sawai Jai Singh II, ruler of the Rajput kingdom of Amber.
